activity.notes: Kintpuash, also known as Captain Jack, was a principal Modoc headman and 1864 treaty signatory. He led Modoc bands resisting forced removal and became the central Modoc war leader in 1872–1873, before his execution on 3 October 1873. ATLAS records his leadership within the Modoc political community rather than treating the Modoc as a centralized state.

sources.title: Kintpuash (Captain Jack) — Oregon Encyclopedia
sources.citation_text: The Oregon Encyclopedia identifies Kintpuash as a principal Modoc headman during the 1860s and early 1870s, a signatory of the 1864 treaty, and leader of Modoc resistance through the 1872–1873 war.

sources.title: Winema and the Modoc War — National Archives
sources.citation_text: The National Archives account documents Kintpuash's leadership of the Modoc group that resisted forced return to the reservation and occupied the Lava Beds in 1872–1873.
